# Morsel

> Morsel is a small, self-hosted, API-first service for creating capability-protected Markdown shares and rendering them in a same-origin web viewer.

The public service URL is `https://morsel.narumi.dev/`. Native OAuth/MCP deployment readiness is not established by this document; the last production `/mcp` probe returned HTTP 404. Complete the deployment handoff before claiming readiness. It supports GitHub Flavored Markdown, syntax-highlighted fenced code, KaTeX, Mermaid, and fenced `vega-lite` charts with inline data. Authored HTML is not executed, and Vega-Lite charts cannot load external resources.

Important usage notes:

- REST creation/revocation requires a UI-managed Bearer API key. MCP accepts that same key or a native OAuth access token, validated in PostgreSQL on every request. Writes stay account-owned; an admin role does not bypass ownership. Cookies, authorization codes, and refresh tokens cannot authorize MCP. OAuth is only for `/mcp`, not REST writes or account management. Existing API keys keep their non-expiring lifetime until revocation and remain valid after account recovery.
- Pi can use `{ "mcpServers": { "morsel": { "url": "https://morsel.narumi.dev/mcp" } } }` at an approved reachable endpoint. An explicit Authorization header disables Pi OAuth; retain custom-header API-key mode as an alternative. Native public DCR uses `token_endpoint_auth_method=none`, S256 PKCE, exact resource `<MORSEL_URL origin>/mcp`, and configured-origin issuer/iss validation. CIMD is deliberately omitted despite the MCP recommendation to avoid client-controlled metadata fetching/SSRF; Morsel fetches no client metadata or callback URLs. Go MCP SDK v1.8.0 needs a resource-aware refresh HTTP transport/NewTokenSource hook; default oauth2.Config.TokenSource omits resource and receives 400. Pi 1.4.0 sends resource.
- OAuth consent shows the account name/UUID, unverified app name/client ID, redirect host, resource, share permissions, and persistent access. Never approve an unsolicited connection. `mcp:shares` covers the three tools; optional `offline_access` permits refresh only. The initial 401 challenge requests both scopes for Pi URL-only refresh. Inspect/revoke only owned connections in Connected apps under `/account`; API keys/OAuth tokens cannot manage them.
- Approval and connected-app revocation require a browser session, exact Origin, CSRF, and passkey verification within twelve hours. Denial does not require fresh verification. No GET/login/preview issues a code. Consent lasts ten minutes and binds the displayed account and exact session; logout, recovery, account switching, or a new session for the same account requires restarting the pending request. Logout does not revoke issued families or API keys; recovery invalidates older OAuth codes/grants/tokens but not API keys.
- Codes last one minute; access tokens at most ten minutes. Offline-access families expire thirty days after approval without sliding extension; access-only families expire ten minutes after approval. Atomic rotation replaces old refresh/access credentials; replay revokes the family including access. A lost code/refresh response is uncertain: never automatically retry redemption. Restart authorization if safe continuation is not possible. PostgreSQL preserves state across restarts. Refresh scope, if supplied, must match the granted canonical scope after order normalization; narrowing and widening both return invalid_scope. Reauthorize without offline_access for no refresh; Pi/configured Go omit scope on refresh.
- Native OAuth runs in the same Go process with Fosite v0.49.0 and patched dependencies. Credentials have 256 random bits and type prefixes `moc_`/`moa_`/`mor_`; only SHA-256 signatures/hashes are stored, never raw OAuth credentials or PKCE verifiers. No HMAC secret or JWT signing keys are required. Existing share rows/backups still contain raw share capabilities and Markdown.
- OAuth registrations expire after ninety days, extended by valid authorization/token traffic. Caps count all retained rows: 10,000 clients/requests/grants, 100 grants per account, 10,000 tokens per family. Cleanup runs at most once per minute per process and deletes at most 2,000 rows per statement; active-family code/refresh tombstones remain until family expiry. Grant rows remain until family expiry; expired access can be pruned. Revocation is not immediate capacity release. Wait for eligible expiry/cleanup and explicitly reauthorize, not an automatic retry loop. The separate OAuth limiter allows 60/source-IP/endpoint-kind/minute and 1,000 globally/minute per process; forwarded IP headers are not trusted.
- `/mcp` provides stateless Streamable HTTP with normal JSON responses, no persistent sessions/session IDs, and no persistent SSE streams. Authenticated GET/DELETE return 405 with `Allow: POST`. The official Go SDK is pinned to v1.8.0; supported/tested protocol versions are `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, and `2025-03-26`.
- MCP POST needs Bearer authorization even for initialization/discovery, JSON Content-Type, and `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. Subsequent requests need the negotiated `MCP-Protocol-Version`. Authority/Host must match `MORSEL_URL` after hostname-case/default-port normalization; use the configured localhost URL for direct development. Omitted Origin is allowed; a present Origin must be exactly the canonical configured origin. Duplicate, null, and foreign Origins are forbidden.
- `tools/list` publishes explicit MCP input/output schemas. `create_share` takes REST creation fields (`content`, optional `expires_in`, `max_views`, `preview`, `telegram_instant_view`); null expiration/view limits mean absent. `get_share` takes `{ "token": "RAW_CAPABILITY_TOKEN" }`, never a URL or UUID. `revoke_share` takes `{ "id": "ADMINISTRATIVE_SHARE_UUID" }` and succeeds with `{ "id": "...", "revoked": true }` only for the validated credential's account; repeated owned revocation succeeds. There are no account, listing, or admin tools.
- Every successful REST `GET /v1/shares/{share}` or MCP `get_share` consumes exactly one view. A valid capability can read another account's share without owner identity. Never retrieve a newly created share to validate it. Retrieve only when explicitly requested; never automatically retry creation or retrieval.
- MCP results contain structured JSON plus matching JSON text. Tool failures use `isError: true` with safe `code`/`message`, distinct from HTTP authentication errors. Missing/invalid credentials receive HTTP 401 with resource_metadata and both scopes; insufficient scope receives 403; authentication storage failures receive safe 503 without fallback. Foreign/missing revocation IDs both use `not_found`; expired, revoked, and exhausted capability errors remain distinct. All MCP responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`; existing body/document/request time limits apply. A deadline before response commitment returns safe HTTP 504. Do not log payloads.
- An opt-in `GET /s/{capability}` Open Graph response does not consume a view, but it repeatedly exposes the explicit preview title and description, optional image URL and locale, and generated share URL; it must not be fetched without the user's request.
- Treat API keys, OAuth codes/tokens/verifiers, raw capability tokens, and complete share URLs as secrets. Do not expose or log them. Pi stores OAuth credentials in `~/.pi/agent/mcp-auth.json` by default; protect that file and do not assume OS keyring storage. Native physical-passkey/browser/callback/storage behavior and untested client compatibility require external checks.
- Viewer URLs use `#/s/{capability}` when preview metadata is omitted. Shares created with required `preview.title` and `preview.description` and optional `preview.image` and `preview.locale` use `/s/{capability}` so link-preview crawlers can fetch metadata; a browser then sends the capability to the same-origin retrieval API.
- Retrieval responses must not be cached. Expired, revoked, and exhausted shares are unavailable.

## Documentation

- [Morsel documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/narumiruna/morsel/main/README.md): Setup, API examples, retrieval semantics, configuration, operations, and security model.
- [MCP usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/narumiruna/morsel/main/docs/usage.md#mcp-clients): URL-only Pi OAuth, the custom-header API-key alternative, retained curl examples, consent/revocation, tool effects, and secret handling. Production proxy and external-client acceptance require the deployment handoff; local tests do not establish them.
- [Morsel OpenAPI contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/narumiruna/morsel/main/packages/server/openapi.yaml): REST and manual OAuth/account request, response, authentication, schema, and error definitions; MCP tool schemas come from authenticated `tools/list`.

- [Morsel source repository](https://github.com/narumiruna/morsel): Go API, React viewer, deployment configuration, tests, and issue history.
